sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
A junglefowl by the name of GALLUS² has taken an interest in you.

The mission Kal'tsit has borne through over ten thousand years of asceticism means nothing to it. It just wants to watch.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A scratch left on your arm. Kal'tsit once traveled with it, but never tamed it. It is a life that struggled through the wilderness, not a docile pet.

sections.title: Basic Info
sections.text:
[Serial Number] GALLUS²
[Model] Junglefowl (self-declared)
[Gender Assignment] Female (self-declared)
[Time in Service] 15 years
[Manufacturer] Another chicken
[Place of Production] A thicket somewhere in eastern Terra
[Date of Release] May 4 (estimated by Kal'tsit from its bone samples)
[Height] 120cm
[Weight] Classified
[Inspection Report]
Outer casing largely intact, structure unstable, durability below standard.
Due to the Operator's fierce resistance, inspection of the chassis could not be completed; data pending.
Due to the Operator's aggressive behavior, inspection of the Arts core could not be completed, though it can be judged to be functioning normally.
During the compilation of this file, the Operator was highly uncooperative, leaving several entries in the file and several figures in the Inspection Report either missing or of doubtful accuracy. The particulars have been reported to the higher-ups, and a re-inspection is pending.

'Reported to the higher-ups'? Cluck? I haven't even gone and told Kal'tsit on you yet. What makes you think it's your turn?
——GALLUS²

sections.title: Profile
sections.text:
An anomalous being that calls itself 'GALLUS².' Its main body is a hut built of metal and glass, held up by claw-shaped metal legs, with a small quantity of organic feathers attached to the rear of the hut and the backs of the legs.
Discovered at the core of the sarcophagus in Zelgrad and confirmed to be a special life form produced by the sarcophagus. It carries intact memories from over ten thousand years ago, most of which concern Kal'tsit.
After the withdrawal from Zelgrad, it followed Kal'tsit back to Rhodes Island, where it assists as a history consultant, a biology consultant, and a field Operator.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
GALLUS² makes no attempt to avoid the subject of the time it spent traveling with Kal'tsit—or rather, it is a little too eager to tell those stories. It claims it spared no effort in fetching every sample Kal'tsit's research required, from soil and rock to plants and insects. It could even, by employing certain 'special methods' (author's note: acting as bait), deliver large predators dozens of times its own size to Kal'tsit entirely unharmed.
But the moment anyone asks what Kal'tsit's 'research' actually was, GALLUS² instantly loses all interest, starts scratching irritably at the floor, and then launches into a tirade.
'What? What is it? I'm telling my story—so what exactly are you listening for? Kal'tsit's "research"? I don't know anything about it, and I don't care. I helped her with all that so I could work out which bugs are easiest for a chicken to digest, which branches make the sturdiest nest once you snap them off, and whose fur keeps a nest warmest once you've plucked it. It took me a mere fifteen years to figure out exactly what the most perfect life for a chicken looks like. Doesn't that make me a great researcher? Shouldn't you be paying attention to my findings?'
Having said all this, it always ends up sweeping its tail feathers listlessly back and forth across the very floor it just finished scratching. Perhaps it has remembered that there is no longer a second chicken like itself; or perhaps it has realized that even it no longer has any need to eat or to build a nest.
This state of affairs lasted for about half a month, until, much to our bewilderment, we found it beginning to frequent the Engineering Department—not merely chasing Closure around demanding to be refitted, but also helping itself to 'gnawing' on every last part stored in the workshop.
When called to account, GALLUS² flatly refused to admit any fault. It hopped proudly onto the top of an air conditioner and delivered the following statement:
'I've got it! My research project now is to test every substance on this land and see what effect each one has on a glass-and-tin chicken with a house on her back! Give me another fifteen years and I'll work out exactly what the most perfect life for a glass-and-tin chicken looks like! Doesn't that make me a great researcher? Shouldn't you all be... (remainder omitted)'
...So be it, then.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Using the blank Originium 'Oka' as a base and the life information preserved within that Originium as its form, the genesis effect of the sarcophagus has a chance of reproducing a life form that once existed. The principle behind GALLUS²'s birth is perfectly clear. And yet, when it and Closure looked into the mirror together, both wore the same baffled expression—
Why a hut?

After repeated comparisons, we confirmed that the hut's form most closely resembles a structure now all but extinct across the vast lands of Ursus—the burden-borne hut once used by the group that calls itself the 'Freemen'—a peculiar structure only half the size of a telephone booth, erected directly upon the back of a burdenbeast.
The odd thing is that these structures are tiny—too small to hold even a single adult—and few in number besides: across the ruins of an entire Freemen tribe, one or two is often all that can be found. If it cannot possibly have been a dwelling, then what role did it play in the life of the Freemen?
We found the answer in the Freemen's curses. 'Grandmother above,' they would say when startled, when angry, and when kicked by a burdenbeast. 'Grandmother,' it seems, was the object of the Freemen's faith—after all, there was no chance they would ever put their faith in the Emperor.
In the legends of the Freemen, the most striking trait of 'Grandmother' is that she always brings along a hut with long legs. 'Grandmother' demands much of the Freemen—their burdenbeasts, their blades and bows, even the spoils they bought with blood. She has them place these things inside the hut, then leads the hut away. Some cursed her as a wicked witch who plundered as she pleased, but more believed that 'Grandmother' had refused death on their behalf, using these things as the price to hold back death's advance. And so the Freemen could walk a few more years, see the spring flowers bloom a few more times, or take to the battlefield a few more times.
And so, every time the Freemen set out for the battlefield, they would offer 'Grandmother' something inside the burden-borne hut, praying that death might come a little later.
Even so, 'Grandmother' was not omnipotent after all. When a man had nothing left to give—his blade already broken three times over, his brothers and sisters buried on as many different battlefields, every last ounce of strength for hatred spent—'Grandmother' would silently move the hut aside and point him to the road that led to death.
'I can hold it back for you no longer.' So said 'Grandmother' at the last.

So, what does any of this have to do with GALLUS²?
Well, the legend of 'Grandmother' had to come from somewhere, didn't it? At the very earliest, back when the Freemen were still bleeding for the great founding of Ursus, songs already told of a witch who walked alongside them and treated their illnesses and wounds. The witch often told stories to the children of the tribes, and the one she told most often was 'The Hut with Long Legs.'
'The Hut with Long Legs Defeats the Monster,' 'The Hut with Long Legs Seeks a Home'—generation after generation of children grew up listening to these stories, and generation after generation of Freemen came to remember that hut with long legs.
Who that witch was, and what the hut in her stories was modeled on, is surely not hard to guess. In view of the sensitivity of the information, we shall set it down only thus: she was a Feline dressed in green, and the hut she spoke of had the claws of a chicken.
